game: SF @ TB Week 6 2025, kickoff 2025-10-12 16:25 ET, TB -3.5, total 46.5, outdoors, weather not saved

script.base: TB is a short home favorite (implied 25.0-21.5) in a competitive outdoor game, not a blowout. Mayfield throws to Egbuka, already the usage king with Evans and Godwin out, against an SF defense that blitzes only 23% and bleeds the middle. White, with Irving and Williams out, is the late-clock back. SF, Purdy out and Mac Jones only questionable, leans on CMC plus Bourne and Tonges rather than a vertical passing game.
script.flip1: Mac Jones plays and CMC controls the game, SF stays in front, TB abandons the run, and White's carries die while Egbuka's targets rise.
script.flip2: TB scores early, the SF backup QB cannot answer, TB runs White and Tucker and caps Egbuka under 85.5; unsaved outdoor weather could also cut explosives.

TB corners McCollum and Morrison Out, Izien Questionable — helps SF pass-catchers, but the QB outs offset that. Sources: pack nflverse injury report and weeks 3-5 logs.

data_check.notes: No sims and no Pinnacle no-vig in the pack, so step 8 cannot price a rung. Stand-in lines are season medians: White 17.5 and Egbuka 85.5 sit on those medians, which is not independent market confirmation. Recent means agree with both overs (White 23.3 rush yds/g in a timeshare; Egbuka 116.3 rec yds/g). Season-median equality is why this is flagged to the human rather than sized. Not cut: the White read is a role change the median does not contain, and the Egbuka read is matchup plus a three-game surge. Model_p values are form proxies, not projections, and both are kept under 0.70. CMC rush under 55.5 would have agreed with form (last4 55, 52, 49, 57 vs a 3.90 YPC defense) but loses to the Purdy-out volume flip, so it is not a second leg. Bourne's 142-yard game is the fluke the checklist says to fade.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and both lost. White finished at 14 because Tucker took a surprising share of Irving's 13 carries a game and SF's interior, with Collins and Davis active, stuffed a 2.8 YPC back. Egbuka finished at 71 because TB led by two scores, Mayfield checked down to Otton and White, and the one explosive SF usually allows went to Shepard. The 85.5 number only needs a quiet WR1 day, and he already has a 29 and an 85 on the sheet. That counter is real, but it requires both a committee and a blowout the 3.5 spread does not forecast, so the legs stay.
slip_story: One TB modest-lead story: new lead back runs (White rushyds over) and the WR1 still gets his against a passive, middle-bleeding defense (Egbuka recyds over). They win together if TB's offense functions in a one-score game. Do not add a total under, an SF rush over, or a second market on either player. Two legs, no TDs. CMC, Bourne and Tonges are the SF stack and need Mac Jones active — left off until inactives.
